_comment: Source-of-truth English strings for runstrict.com localization. The build script (build-i18n.js) substitutes each VALUE (exact English substring, tag-anchored where short) with the matching value from <locale>.json to generate /<locale>/index.html. Brand terms (RunStrict, FLAME, WAVE, CHAOS, The Void, App Store, Google Play, Wear OS, Apple Watch) are intentionally NOT in this catalog and stay untranslated.
meta_title: RunStrict — GPS Running Game | Capture Territory. Dominate Your City.
meta_description: The GPS running game where your footsteps capture territory. Run through hexes, conquer your city, and race The Void before the 40-day season resets. Live now — 1,200+ active runners and growing.
og_description: Turn your daily run into territorial warfare. Flip hexes, conquer your city, and beat The Void. 40-day seasons. Live now — join 1,200+ runners.
twitter_description: Turn your daily run into territorial warfare. Flip hexes, conquer your city, beat The Void. Live now.
og_image_alt: RunStrict GPS running game — capture hexagonal territory
hero_sub:
A location-based running game where your footsteps become territory.
            Choose your team. Flip hexes. Conquer your city — before the season ends.
athlete_sub:
RunStrict turns your daily run into territorial warfare. Hit the streets, flip hexes,
            and conquer your city before The Void wipes the scoreboard.
showcase_sub: Actual gameplay. Real hexes. Real runners. Real war.
how_sub: Every run is a battle. Every step is a claim.
step1_p:
Open RunStrict and hit the streets. GPS tracks every step in real-time. Keep your pace under 12 min/km to
            activate hex capture.
step2_p:
Every ~175m hexagonal tile you run through flips to your team's color. The last runner wins. Speed counts.
            Consistency matters.
step3_p:
Hexes roll up into provinces, countries, regions and continents. Zoom out and the map names the province
            that holds each region — and flies the flag of the nation that holds each continent.
step4_p:
Every hex you cross is new ground, yours, or theirs. Your team's split of 10 points decides what each one
            pays — FLAME bets on enemy hexes, WAVE on its own, CHAOS on the untouched.
void_p:
When the 40-day season ends, every point, rank and team pick is wiped. The map is not. The land remembers
            who ran it last — so no season starts on empty ground.
teams_sub: Every team splits the same 10 points across three kinds of ground. Pick the split that matches how you run.
team_red_desc:
Built to take ground. An enemy hex is worth 6 points to a FLAME runner — the biggest single
            score in the game. Your own streets pay almost nothing, so keep pushing into theirs.
team_blue_desc:
Built to hold ground. Running a hex your team already owns pays 6 — once per hex per day —
            so WAVE wins by showing up every day on the same streets, together.
team_purple_desc:
Built to go where no one has run. A hex nobody has ever touched is worth 6 to CHAOS. The map
            remembers every season, so untouched ground only gets rarer — and more valuable.
rule1_p: Choose FLAME, WAVE or CHAOS when you register. Your team is locked until The Void.
rule2_h: Your hexes pay once a day.
rule2_p: Re-running ground your team already holds scores once per hex per day. New and enemy hexes score every run.
rule3_p: The map carries over between seasons, so a hex only counts as new ground until the first runner in history crosses it.
season_sub: Real-time territory control. Every run matters.
feat1_p: 25 km/h cap. Accelerometer verification. GPS ≤50m accuracy. No spoofing. Real runs only.
feat2_p: 0.5 Hz GPS polling. No WebSocket drains. Data syncs only on launch, resume, and run completion.
feat3_p: CV-based Stability Score rewards steady runners. Green ≥80. Yellow ≥50. Red means chaos.
feat4_p: Province, District, Zone scopes. Your rank means something — and it resets every 40 days.
feat5_p:
No runner IDs in hex data. Who holds what is shown by team color, province name and nation flag — never by
            person.
feat6_p:
Uber's H3 at resolution 9 — ~175m hexagons that roll up into provinces, countries, regions and continents.
            One grid, the whole planet.
testi_sub: From beta runners who haven’t stopped since Season 1.
testi1_q:
“I started waking up at 5am just to capture the park near my office before
            anyone else. I’ve never been this consistent in my life. RunStrict broke my brain in the best way.”
testi2_q:
“Our whole district coordinates runs every evening now. We reclaimed 40 hexes
            in one night. The group chat is on fire. This is the most social I’ve been in years.”
testi3_q:
“I picked CHAOS on day one. Untouched ground is worth 6 to us, so I plan
            routes through streets nobody has ever run. The map remembers every season — I’m racing the whole
            city to the last blank hexes.”
faq_sub: Everything you need to know before your first run.
faq1_a:
RunStrict is a location-based GPS running game where your physical runs capture hexagonal territory tiles
              on a real map of your city. Choose a team — FLAME, WAVE, or CHAOS — flip hexes, and battle for dominance
              before the 40-day season resets in The Void.
faq2_a:
GPS tracks your route in real-time. Every ~175m hexagonal tile you physically run through flips to your
              team’s color. The last runner through a hex holds it. Keep your pace under 12 min/km to activate capture
              mode. No spoofing — accelerometer verification blocks cheaters.
faq4_a:
The Void is the season-end reset every 40 days. All points, rankings and team picks are wiped, and
              everyone chooses a team again. The map itself is not reset — the land remembers its last runner — so the
              next season starts on contested ground, and truly untouched hexes only get rarer.
faq5_a: Every team splits the same 10 points across three kinds of hex. FLAME if you like to attack — an enemy hex pays 6, new ground 3, your own 1. WAVE if you like to hold — your own hexes pay 6 (once per hex per day), new ground 3, enemy 1. CHAOS if you like to explore — a hex nobody has ever run pays 6, everything else 2. You pick once when you register; the choice is locked until The Void.
faq10_a:
Every hex you cross is one of three kinds: new ground (nobody has ever run it), a friendly hex (your team
              already holds it) or an enemy hex. Your team’s table sets the points — FLAME 3 / 1 / 6, WAVE 3 / 6 / 1,
              CHAOS 6 / 2 / 2 for new / friendly / enemy. Friendly hexes pay once per hex per day; new and enemy hexes
              pay every run. No multipliers, no buffs — the table is the whole rule.
faq11_a:
Not during a season. You choose FLAME, WAVE or CHAOS when you register and the choice is locked until The
              Void. Every new season starts with a fresh choice among all three.
faq12_q: Who owns a region or a continent?
faq12_a:
Hexes roll up into provinces, countries, regions and continents, settled every night at midnight GMT+2.
              Team color always shows who holds a hex. Zoom out to a region and the map names the home province of the
              runners holding the most ground there; zoom out to a continent and it flies the flag of the nationality
              holding the most. Ties keep yesterday’s owner. Nothing is ever shown per person.
faq6_a:
RunStrict supports iOS 15+ (iPhone) and Android 10+. GPS accuracy ≤50m is required for hex capture. The
              app uses battery-optimized 0.5 Hz GPS polling, so it won’t drain your battery on long runs.
faq7_q: How is RunStrict different from Strava or Nike Run Club?
faq7_a:
Strava and Nike Run Club focus on personal fitness tracking — distance, pace, heart rate. RunStrict adds a
              competitive territory-capture game layer on top of your runs. Every run is a strategic move in a team-based
              territorial war where you flip hex tiles, score by your team’s doctrine, and compete on tiered
              leaderboards. Think of it as Strava meets Risk.
faq8_q: Is RunStrict like Pokemon GO for runners?
faq8_a:
RunStrict shares the location-based concept but requires actual running with pace verification (under
              12 min/km). There are no virtual creatures — you're capturing real territory tiles on a city map through
              physical athletic effort. Anti-cheat measures including accelerometer verification ensure only real runs
              count.
dl_p:
A new season starts every 40 days — every point is up for grabs.
The Void comes for everyone. Don't start the next one from behind.
